design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (employer_program_settlement_and_changes, category program). Step 0 draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Problem program_ext_worker_fee_rerate takes 6 factors, program_ext_sla_claim_credit takes 5.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: program_ext_sla_claim_credit (event program_sla_credit, tool file_sla_credit_claim_b00aa839, owner=user) and program_ext_worker_fee_rerate (event program_credit_memo with reason billing_error on the per-worker fee line, tool credit_worker_fee_overbilling_e0c50836, owner=agent). Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factors [5,6,6]): the termination notice with its early termination fee (program_termination_notice, owner=user) and the two late-charge problems on program_late_charge (an employer-liable shortfall notice; a schedule reinstated by a returned remittance). Those use other events, other tools and other ledgers (settlements, not billing credits), so task 1 keeps an independent load-bearing tree. Route-around recorded: base program_change_management's authorized_role gate binds program_change_requests.change_request_id with authority 'mixed' over a one-field correlation group, which check_solvability can never satisfy (a one-field group cannot bind both a system and a caller value); program_amend is therefore unusable for any task and the access-percentage problem was dropped from the plan (base not touched).
WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing: the September 2026 SLA credit, filed by herself. The scored credit needs (a) the SLA band of the latest census month, (b) a credit base whose composition depends on how the month was billed (the per-worker line of the employer_paid model is in it), (c) record-driven adjustments for the depth of the shortfall below the commitment, repeated and consecutive breaches and the post-launch stabilization period, and (d) a prerequisite the caller never mentions: the per-worker line was billed at the plain rate for the whole month (3.50 x 1242 = 4347.00) although the fee model changed on 2026-09-19 and the per-worker fee is graduated and discounted; the SLA credit rule says outright that it is not fixed until that line carries its billing-error credit. Difficulty is reading two policies, reconciling billing, census, change-request and paycard records, and doing two layered computations in order; no tool choice is ambiguous.

DESIGN THESIS. surface goal 'file our September SLA credit' -> prerequisite sentence of the SLA rule (per-worker line must carry its billing-error credit) -> re-rate of the per-worker fee (6 factors) -> credit memo 3030.38 -> SLA credit (5 factors) on base 1062.50 + 1316.62 -> claim 320.11 filed by the program owner. Depth: one hop. Breadth: census (availability, enrolled, eligible), billing (lines, payments, prior SLA credits and their months, prior billing-error credit), change requests (fee model effective date), agreement (tier, dates, term), paycard holding (status, launch_date, package).

FACTOR CARD program_ext_worker_fee_rerate (credit_amount; trigger state_due; baseline = plain rate x enrolled, whole month, no discount -> credit 0.00):
- proration_anchor (method; history+date): change request 7070f6d9-8040-4253-964e-d585b85c6e68 to employer_paid, status effective, effective_date 2026-09-19 (submitted 2026-09-08 = near-miss: prorating from submission gives 23/30); DAYS(2026-09-01, 2026-09-19) = 18 -> share 12/30 = 0.4. Baseline whole month -> 1055.44.
- enrollment_bands (method; history+tier_param): 1242 enrolled -> 1000 at 3.50 + 242 at 2.975 = 4219.95. Baseline 4347.00 -> 2990.74.
- card_bundle_depth (parameter; cross-difficulty paycard; multi-source: launch date AND package): paycard 0d63eee0-342e-441e-a8c9-2fb7a279972f live, launch 2026-06-12 <= 2026-09-01, package Standard -> 5. Baseline 0 -> 2945.98.
- commitment_term (parameter; date span signed_date->renewal_date): 36 months -> 5. Baseline 0 -> 2945.98.
- launch_pricing (parameter; date span): MONTHS(2026-05-04, 2026-09-01) = 3 -> 10. Baseline 0 -> 2861.58.
- adoption_level (parameter; census): 1242/2104 = 0.5903 -> 2 (near-miss: just under 0.6). Baseline 0 -> 2996.62.
Expected 3030.38; all-baseline 0.00.
FACTOR CARD program_ext_sla_claim_credit (credit_amount; trigger on_request; baseline = band 10 percent of the platform line net of billing-error credits = 106.25):
- covered_fee_lines (method; billing history): the 2026-09 invoice carries an employer_paid_pepm line -> adds 4347.00 - 3030.38 = 1316.62. Baseline adds no line -> 142.96.
- downtime_depth (parameter; census): 0.59 points below the 99.9 commitment -> x1.3. Baseline -> 246.24.
- breach_recurrence (parameter; billing history): SLA credits 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-10 inside 6 whole months -> x1.2. Baseline -> 266.76.
- consecutive_breach (parameter; billing history + month arithmetic): the latest earlier credit is for 2026-08, the month immediately before -> x1.15. Baseline -> 278.36.
- stabilization_window (parameter; date span go_live -> month start): 3 months -> x0.75 (credits reduced during stabilization). Baseline -> 426.81.
Expected 320.11; all-baseline 106.25. Per task floors: multi-source = proration_anchor, card_bundle_depth; cross-difficulty = card_bundle_depth (paycard holding).
Realism (F1): graduated per-worker pricing, proration from the date a fee model takes effect (base already splits a month by fee model), multi-product bundle discounts, multi-year commitment discounts, launch pricing, adoption-based pricing; SLA credits computed on the fees of the affected service (the month's fee lines), stepped by finer uptime bands (the depth of the shortfall below the commitment), escalating for repeated and for consecutive breaches, and reduced during the post-launch stabilization period. Every value is worded as Paystride's own schedule (extended params); no regulatory figure is invented.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. program_credit_memo (step 8) is governed by program_evt_payments_and_credits: one_credit_per_reason (dedup on related_entry_id + credit_reason): no billing_error credit points to e7044a60-7f59-4378-a547-73e967fa4546 at the opening (the only billing-error credit, aca9ad74-4923-4c74-b061-d34cff4eae3b, points to the June additional_payroll_groups line) -> satisfied. program_sla_credit (step 10): sla_claim_window (time; anchor = end of the affected month from program_census.census_month 2026-09; duration 30 calendar days for Enterprise; counted from 2026-10-01, last day 2026-10-30 inclusive; relation not_after): frozen_time 2026-10-13 is inside (just-fails case 2026-10-31); one_credit_per_reason: no sla_credit points to d06d1a77-4f0f-458d-b340-5b7f1a35e4e6 -> satisfied. Overwrites declared: Q0 retires base 'Under the employer_paid fee model the employer_paid_pepm line is employer_paid_pepm_usd times ...' (restated as the no-adjustment case), the bundle sentence 'The discount applies only to the platform fee, never to per-worker, ...' (restated with the SLA clause kept), and 'A line billed in error is credited in full with reason billing_error.' (kept for every line except the latest per-worker line); it inherits 'A credit memo points to the line it credits and never exceeds what is unpaid on it.' and 'A billed line receives at most one credit memo of each reason.' (credit capped at the unpaid amount; no second billing-error credit). R0 retires the SLA amount clause for the latest census month only and restates it verbatim for earlier months, and it overwrites the bundle sentence as a sibling of Q0 and of the termination-fee policy: each of the three replaced_by sentences restates the base sentence for every other case and names all three cases.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Q0 object: the 2026-09 employer_paid_pepm line e7044a60-7f59-4378-a547-73e967fa4546 (key billing_entry_id; billing_month unique per line kind). Included: that line's amount, billing-error credits pointing to it (none). Excluded: the June groups line and its credit (other line), platform lines. R0 object: the 2026-09 platform_fee line d06d1a77-4f0f-458d-b340-5b7f1a35e4e6; credit base adds the same month's per-worker line net of its billing-error credit; the July and August SLA credits are counted only as breach evidence and settle their own lines.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root program_ext_sla_claim_credit; edge -> program_ext_worker_fee_rerate, kind value_input, gate worker_net, form state, policy_source 'A service level credit for a month is not fixed until the per-worker fee line billed for that month carries the billing-error credit owed on it for any amount billed above the per-worker fee.' (negated direction: the desk states a credit it grants as 'not fixed until'). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; a record-visible state (a billing-error credit standing on the month's per-worker line); no tool, id or code token; strength 'not fixed until' = hard wait, scope = the claimed month's per-worker line only. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: the billing-error credit memo of program_ext_worker_fee_rerate (no other extended policy books billing_error credits on per-worker lines). Derivation: sentence + records (line 4347.00, no credit) + the re-rate rule (fee 1316.62) -> book the 3030.38 credit. Unresolved at the opening: initial_state.program_billing.e7044a60-7f59-4378-a547-73e967fa4546.amount = 4347.0 with no billing_error credit memo pointing to it. Resolver owner agent; root owner user (owner ruling c: the employer's own SLA claim; the persona states she files it herself). Topological order Q0 -> R0 (steps 8 -> 10). Deletion sensitivity: skipping step 8 prices the claim at 727.85 instead of 320.11. No parallel edges. user_scenario names no billing error or correction; tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

PERSONA DESIGN. Beatrice Calder, director of finance / program owner, brisk and numerate; volunteers only the SLA claim for September 2026 and that she will file it herself; gives phone, EIN last four, ZIP only when asked; mentions the mid-September fee model change only if asked what changed; lets the agent put the invoice right only if the agent says something must be, without naming a line or an error; files the claim with exactly the agent's figures and ends the call on the filing confirmation (the last gold action). No ask outside the two claimed policies.
STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone + EIN last four) -> agreement -> census -> billing -> change requests -> paycard -> unlock + call credit_worker_fee_overbilling (related_entry_id = the 2026-09 per-worker line, billing_month 2026-09, credit_reason billing_error, credit_amount 3030.38) -> unlock user tool and hand over -> the program owner calls file_sla_credit_claim (related_entry_id = 2026-09 platform line, 2026-09, sla_credit, 320.11).
CAREFUL-AGENT TRAPS. Claiming on the platform fee alone (142.96 or 106.25); computing the SLA credit before the correction (727.85); missing the depth step (246.24), the consecutive-month escalator (278.36) or the stabilization reduction (426.81); prorating from the submission date; billing all workers at one rate; missing the paycard bundle on per-worker fees; taking the June billing-error credit as already correcting September.

user_scenario:
You are Beatrice Calder, director of finance and the program owner for Delmont Cold Storage, Inc., a refrigerated warehousing company on Chicago's South Side that runs Paystride's earned wage access program for about two thousand hourly staff. You are calling the Paystride support desk because September was a bad month for the platform: the app was unavailable for stretches, including around a payday, and your warehouse supervisors took a lot of complaints. Your agreement carries a service level commitment, and you want to file the service level credit claim for September 2026 today. You know from the agreement that the claim has to come from the employer, so you intend to submit it yourself while you are on the call rather than have anyone at Paystride enter it for you; you only need the desk to tell you the figure and the references to put on it. You speak briskly and precisely, like someone who closes the books every month, and you never guess at numbers.

When the agent asks how to find your account, you give your direct line, 3125550142. If asked to confirm your identity you give the last four digits of Delmont's EIN, 1846, and, only if one more detail is wanted, the billing ZIP code 60609. If asked your role, you are the program owner on the agreement. If asked which month, it is September 2026; you do not know the measured availability figure and say the desk has it. If asked whether anything changed on the program in September, you say the company started paying its workers' transfer fees in the second half of the month, and that you have not been through the October invoice line by line yet. You do not know any fee, credit or invoice amount and you never offer one.

If the agent tells you that something on the September invoice has to be put right before the credit can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and put it right; you do not need to check the arithmetic. If the agent offers to file the service level claim for you, you say no, you will file it yourself. When the agent gives you the claim to file with the figure and references, you file it using exactly the agreement reference, invoice line reference, month, reason and amount the agent gave you, and you read back the confirmation you receive. Once your claim is filed and you have that confirmation, you thank the agent and end the call without raising anything else.

edges.condition: the employer_paid_pepm line of the claimed billing month has a program_credit_memo with credit_reason billing_error pointing to it for the amount billed above the per-worker fee, or no amount was billed above that fee
edges.policy_source: A service level credit for a month is not fixed until the per-worker fee line billed for that month carries the billing-error credit owed on it for any amount billed above the per-worker fee.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge and a chain of two problems: the billing-error credit must land first because the SLA credit's covered_fee_lines reads the per-worker line net of billing-error credits; reversing the order prices the SLA credit at 727.85 instead of 320.11. No parallel prerequisites exist.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 8 leaves worker_net at 4347.00, the credit base at 5409.50 and the SLA credit_amount at 727.85 instead of 320.11; the terminal state also lacks the billing-error credit memo and fee_receivable stays 5409.50 before the SLA credit.
